name: ChatGPT
description: The most widely used AI assistant, with a free tier covering everyday coding and writing help.
long_description: ChatGPT handles explanation, drafting, debugging and analysis, with file uploads, web browsing and code execution depending on plan. The free tier includes access to current models with usage caps.
free_access_summary: Free tier with capped access to current models, browsing and file uploads.
not_ideal_for: Deep repository-wide context without extra tooling

free_access.description: Free tier with message caps on the most capable models, falling back to a smaller model.
restrictions: Usage caps reset on a rolling window
Some features limited to paid plans

name: Claude
tagline: Assistant strong at long code context
description: Anthropic's assistant, well regarded for reasoning over large codebases and long documents.
long_description: Claude handles long context well, which suits reviewing large files, analysing documents and multi-step reasoning. It supports artifacts for iterating on code and MCP connectors for external tools. A free tier is available with daily limits.
free_access_summary: Free tier with daily message limits that reset each day.
not_ideal_for: Heavy usage on the free tier - limits arrive quickly

free_access.description: Daily message allowance that resets; limits depend on demand.
restrictions: Some models restricted to paid plans

name: Google Gemini
description: Assistant with large context windows, deep research and integration with Google services.
long_description: Gemini handles text, images, audio and video with very large context windows, and connects to Google Workspace. A free tier is available to anyone with a Google account.
free_access_summary: Free tier with daily usage limits on the most capable models.
best_for: Analysing large documents or codebases in one prompt
not_ideal_for: Unlimited use of top models for free

restrictions: Some features require a paid plan

name: DeepSeek
description: Strong coding and reasoning models with open weights and a free web assistant.
long_description: DeepSeek publishes open weight models that perform competitively on coding and mathematics benchmarks, which can be self-hosted or accessed through a low-cost API. The web assistant is free.
free_access_summary: Web assistant is free and model weights are openly published; API usage is metered.
not_ideal_for: Organisations with restrictions on the provider's jurisdiction

free_access.description: Model weights are openly licensed and the web assistant is free.
restrictions: Self-hosting large models needs serious hardware

name: Mistral Le Chat
description: Assistant from Mistral AI with a free tier and a family of open weight models.
long_description: Le Chat provides fast responses, code assistance and document analysis, backed by models that Mistral also publishes in open weight form for self-hosting. A free tier is available.
free_access_summary: Free tier with generous daily usage; several model weights are openly licensed.
best_for: Teams wanting open weights with a hosted option
not_ideal_for: Workloads needing the largest proprietary models

free_access.description: Free tier with daily message limits.
restrictions: Advanced features require a paid plan

name: Perplexity
description: Search-first assistant that answers with linked sources, with a usable free tier.
long_description: Perplexity grounds answers in live web results and shows citations, which makes it verifiable in a way general chatbots are not. The free tier includes unlimited basic searches and a few advanced ones per day.
free_access_summary: Unlimited basic searches plus a small daily allowance of advanced Pro searches.
best_for: Checking current library behaviour and release notes

free_access.description: Unlimited quick searches plus a limited number of advanced Pro searches per day.

name: Phind
description: Search assistant tuned for programming questions, returning code with sources.
long_description: Phind targets technical queries specifically, pulling from documentation and StackOverflow-style sources and returning working code with explanations. A free tier covers everyday use.
free_access_summary: Free tier with a daily allowance of searches.

restrictions: Advanced model access is limited on the free tier

name: NotebookLM
description: Upload documents and get answers, summaries and audio overviews strictly from those sources.
long_description: NotebookLM answers only from the material you provide and cites the exact passage, which largely eliminates hallucination for document work. It also generates podcast-style audio overviews. It is free with a Google account.
free_access_summary: Free with a Google account, with limits on notebooks and sources per notebook.
not_ideal_for: Questions that need information beyond your uploads

free_access.description: Free tier with caps on notebooks, sources per notebook and daily queries.
restrictions: Higher limits require a paid Google AI plan

name: Elicit
description: Finds and summarises academic papers, extracting structured data across many studies at once.
long_description: Elicit searches a large corpus of academic papers and builds comparison tables of findings, methods and populations. Free accounts receive a monthly credit allowance.
free_access_summary: Monthly free credit allowance for searching and summarising papers.

name: Consensus
description: Search engine that answers questions using conclusions from peer-reviewed research.
long_description: Consensus surfaces what studies actually concluded on a question, with an indication of agreement across the literature. A free tier allows a limited number of AI-assisted searches per month.
free_access_summary: Free tier with unlimited basic searches and a monthly allowance of AI features.

free_access.description: Unlimited searches with a monthly cap on AI-generated summaries.

name: Semantic Scholar
description: Free academic search engine with an open API covering hundreds of millions of papers.
long_description: Run by the Allen Institute for AI, Semantic Scholar offers AI-generated paper summaries, citation context and a genuinely free API that developers can build on, with an optional higher-rate key.
free_access_summary: Free to use and free to call via the public API; a free key raises rate limits.
best_for: Building research tools on free data

free_access.description: Free access to the site and a public API with rate limits.
restrictions: Higher limits require requesting a key

name: Otter.ai
description: Records and transcribes meetings, producing summaries and action items automatically.
long_description: Otter joins calls, transcribes in real time and extracts decisions and action items, which is useful for keeping a searchable record of standups and design discussions. A free plan includes monthly transcription minutes.
free_access_summary: Free plan with a monthly transcription minute allowance and a per-conversation limit.
best_for: Keeping a record of technical discussions
not_ideal_for: Long daily meeting volumes on the free plan

free_access.description: Monthly transcription minutes on the free plan.

name: Obsidian
description: Markdown notes stored as plain files on your machine, extensible with AI plugins.
long_description: Obsidian keeps notes as local Markdown files with backlinks and a graph view, and its plugin ecosystem adds AI assistance including fully local models. Personal use is free.
free_access_summary: Free for personal use with no account required; files stay on your machine.
best_for: Engineering notes and documentation you own

free_access.description: Free for personal use, including commercial use by individuals.
restrictions: Sync and publish services are paid

name: Excalidraw
tagline: Diagrams from text or hand sketches
description: Open source whiteboard with text-to-diagram generation, ideal for architecture sketches.
long_description: Excalidraw produces hand-drawn style diagrams that are quick to read in design documents, and can generate diagrams from a text description or Mermaid syntax. It is MIT licensed and self-hostable.
free_access_summary: MIT licensed, free to use in the browser or self-hosted.

free_access.description: Free and open source; the hosted editor requires no account.
restrictions: Team features on the hosted plus plan are paid
